Adelic and Classical Modular Forms for GL(2)
Adelic and Classical Modular Forms for GL(2). An exposition of the translation between classical modular forms and automorphic forms on the adelic group $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$. Provides a geometric interpretation of modular forms as sections of line bundles over modular curves, along with minimal ad hoc constructions of Eisenstein series. Details the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb{R})$ with basis elements $Z, H, Y_+, Y_-$, where the center $\mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ of the universal enveloping algebra is isomorphic to a polynomial ring in two generators. Explores the space of bases $B$ of $\mathbb{C}$ as a real vector space, identifying it as an open subset of $\mathbb{C}^2$ with commuting left and right actions by $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathbb{C})$. The right action of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is complex analytic and gives an identification with the upper half-plane $\mathcal{H}^{\pm} \times \mathbb{C}^\times$ via $(\tau, z) \mapsto \left(\frac{a\tau+c}{b\tau+d}, (b\tau+d)z\right)$. Examines the complexified Lie algebra tangent space decomposition into holomorphic and anti-holomorphic subspaces, the subspace $V_i \subset \mathfrak{gl}_2$, and the bijection $B/\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathcal{L}$ with the moduli of discrete rank-2 lattices. Covers moderate growth conditions, smooth adelic automorphic forms, and representations invariant under right translation by $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_f)$.

Class Field Theory and Noncommutative Geometry
Class Field Theory and Noncommutative Geometry. An exposition by Alain Connes on class field theory through the lens of the adèle class space $X_{\mathbb{Q}} = \mathbb{Q}^\times \backslash \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}}$. Abelian extensions of a number field $K$ are encoded internally by its idele class group $C_K = \mathbb{A}_K^\times / K^\times$, acting as a Galois group of the maximal abelian extension via Artin reciprocity. Galois actions on roots are realized through group actions on spaces. The quotient space $X_K = K^\times \backslash \mathbb{A}_K$ is ergodic with respect to the Haar measure, serving as a prototype noncommutative space (leaf space of a foliation). Translates local-to-global class field theory via the inclusion of local isotropy groups $K_v^\times \hookrightarrow C_K$. Connects the Riemann–Weil explicit formulas $\sum_v \int f(u)/|1-u|\,d^*u$ to a trace formula for the scaling operator on the adèle class space. Introduces the scaling site $X_{\mathbb{Q}} = \mathbb{Q}^\times \backslash \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}} / \widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^\times$, modeled as a noncommutative space of rank-1 subgroups of $\mathbb{R}$, where periodic orbits of length $\log p$ correspond to prime numbers $p$, realizing the Frobenius endomorphism as a mapping torus. Relates this construction to Grothendieck's étale fundamental group $\pi_1^{\text{ét}}$ and the 3D topology of $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}$.

Maximal Abelian Extensions Unramified Outside S
Maximal Abelian Extensions Unramified Outside S. Discussion and computation of the maximal abelian extension $K_S^{\text{ab}}$ of a number field $K$ unramified outside a finite set of places $S$. For a singleton prime $S = \{p\}$, $K_S^{\text{ab}}$ is given by the direct limit of ray class fields modulo $\mathfrak{p}^n \mathcal{O}_K$. Explains ramification at infinite places and the Galois group $G_S(K)^{\text{ab}} = G_S(K) / \overline{[G_S(K), G_S(K)]}$. Details the connection to class field theory, Poitou–Tate duality, and the Kronecker–Weber theorem for $K = \mathbb{Q}$.

Comprehensive Glossary of Algebraic Geometry
Comprehensive Glossary of Algebraic Geometry. A 46-page reference dictionary compiling core definitions and theorems: - **Abelian Categories & Additivity:** Categories equipped with biproducts $\bigoplus$, kernels, cokernels, and the first isomorphism theorem $\operatorname{Coim}(f) \cong \operatorname{Im}(f)$. Semiadditive categories satisfy $\coprod \cong \prod$, yielding semiring structures on endomorphism sets $\operatorname{End}(X)$. - **Ampleness & Positivity:** A line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ on a projective scheme $X$ is very ample if it admits a closed immersion $X \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}_A^n$ defined by global sections; ample if $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes m}$ is very ample for some $m > 0$. Base-point freeness means global sections generate the stalks $\mathcal{L}_x$ everywhere. - **Divisors & Canonical Sheaves:** Cartier divisors are global sections of $\mathcal{K}_X^\times / \mathcal{O}_X^\times$. Weil divisors $\sum n_i Y_i$ are formal integer linear combinations of codimension-1 prime subvarieties. The canonical bundle $\omega_X = \det(\Omega_{X/k}^1)$ is the top exterior power of Kähler differentials, acting as the dualizing sheaf in Serre duality. - **Morphisms & Flatness:** Flat morphisms preserve exact sequences under tensor products $\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} \mathcal{O}_X$, ensuring constant Hilbert polynomials across fibers. Étale morphisms are smooth of relative dimension 0 (flat and unramified). Proper morphisms are separated, finite type, and universally closed. - **Cohomology & Derived Functors:** Sheaf cohomology groups $H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) = R^i\Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})$ quantify obstructions to gluing local sections into global ones. Flasque and soft sheaves are acyclic, computing Čech cohomology without higher derived corrections.

arxiv.org
Internal Language of Topoi in Algebraic Geometry
Internal Language of Topoi in Algebraic Geometry. Ingo Blechschmidt's slides on the petit and gros Zariski topoi: - **Petit Zariski Topos $\operatorname{Shv}(X)$:** The structure sheaf $\mathcal{O}_X$ internally behaves as a field (or local ring where every non-invertible element is nilpotent). A sheaf of modules $\mathcal{F}$ is locally of finite type if and only if it is internally finitely generated. Coherent sheaves correspond internally to finitely presented modules. - **Gros Zariski Topos $\operatorname{Zar}(S)$:** Represents schemes by their functors of points $\mathbf{Sch}/S \to \mathbf{Set}$. The affine line $\mathbb{A}^1$ behaves internally as a commutative field where every function $\mathbb{A}^1 \to \mathbb{A}^1$ is a polynomial. Group schemes $\mathbb{G}_a, \mathbb{G}_m, \mathrm{GL}_n$ appear internally as standard algebraic groups.

Noncommutative Geometry and Fundamental Physics
Noncommutative Geometry and Fundamental Physics. Alain Connes' landmark survey detailing: - **Quantum Variables:** Real variables correspond to self-adjoint operators in Hilbert space; infinitesimals correspond to compact operators. - **Metric Structures:** Distance formula $d(p, q) = \sup \{|f(p) - f(q)| : \|[D, f]\| \le 1\}$, where the line element $ds = D^{-1}$ is the fermion propagator. - **Thermodynamics & Time:** Noncommutativity implies a canonical 1-parameter automorphism group $\delta_t \in \operatorname{Out}(\mathcal{A})$ via the Tomita–Takesaki KMS condition. - **Bost-Connes System:** Exhibits spontaneous symmetry breaking at critical temperature $\beta = 1$ with the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(\beta)$ as the partition function.

Geometry of the Adele Class Space: Part I
Geometry of the Adele Class Space: Part I. Alain Connes' lecture exploring: - **Number Fields & Schemes:** Unifying number rings $\mathcal{O}_K$, function fields $\mathbb{F}_q(C)$, and Riemann surfaces as 1-dimensional regular schemes. - **Galois Theory & Etale Topology:** Separable algebras, traces, finite étale morphisms, and why $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}$ behaves as a simply connected 3-manifold where primes are knots. - **Topos Semantics:** Topoi allow groups/monoids to act naturally. The topos $([0, \infty) \rtimes \mathbb{N}^\times)$ computes points over the Boolean semifield $\mathbb{B} = \{0,1\}$, recovering the adèle class space.
youtube.com
Geometry of the Adele Class Space: Part II
Geometry of the Adele Class Space: Part II. Alain Connes' second lecture: - **Adèles & Global Fields:** Global fields sit discretely and cocompactly in their locally compact adèle rings $\mathbb{A}_K$. - **Trace Formulas & Absorption Spectra:** The scaling action on $K_v$ has Schwartz kernel $\delta(y - \lambda x)$ with trace $\int \delta(x - \lambda x)\,dx = 1/|1-\lambda|$. Zeros of $L$-functions emerge as an absorption spectrum, explaining the minus sign in explicit formulas. - **The Arithmetic Site:** The topos $(\mathbb{N}^\times, \mathbb{Z}_{\max})$ over the tropical semifield $\mathbb{R}_{\max}$ exhibits Frobenius automorphisms $\operatorname{Fr}_\lambda(x) = x^\lambda$, establishing an explicit Riemann–Roch theorem for number fields.

Commutative Algebra in the Stacks Project
Commutative Algebra in the Stacks Project. The foundational 1000+ page reference on commutative algebra: - **Exact Sequences & Finiteness:** Snake lemma connecting homomorphisms, finite presentation criteria, and flatness via Tor vanishing. - **Localizations & Spectra:** Universal property of localizations $S^{-1}R$, prime avoidance, the Zariski spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, and characterization of minimal primes as irreducible components. - **Dimension & Regularity:** Krull dimension, Cohen–Macaulay rings where homological depth equals Krull dimension, and regular local rings ($\dim R = \dim_{\kappa} \mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2$). - **Differentials & Smoothness:** Modules of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{S/R}^1$, the de Rham complex, formally smooth/unramified/étale ring morphisms, and Henselian local rings.

Category Theory in Context
Category Theory in Context. Emily Riehl's foundational textbook covering: - **Preservation, Reflection, Creation:** Functors preserve limits (limit in domain $\implies$ limit in codomain), reflect limits (limit cone in image $\implies$ limit cone in domain), and create limits (limit in codomain $\implies$ unique limit lifting). - **Kan Extensions:** Left Kan extensions $\operatorname{Lan}_K F$ (generalizing colimits) and right Kan extensions $\operatorname{Ran}_K F$ (generalizing limits). Pointwise Kan extensions are computed via limit formulas over comma categories: $\operatorname{Ran}_K F(d) \cong \lim (d/K \to \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{E})$. - **Yoneda & Density:** The Yoneda lemma as a pointwise Kan extension. The co-Yoneda lemma expresses every presheaf as a colimit of representables: $F(c) \cong \operatorname{colim}(\mathcal{C}/c \to \mathcal{C} \to \mathbf{Set})$. - **Codensity Monads:** The right Kan extension of a functor along itself. The codensity monad of $\mathbf{FinSet} \hookrightarrow \mathbf{Set}$ is the ultrafilter monad.

Yi Yu Zhang
Yi Yu Zhang, Introduction to equivariant cohomology and the equivariant first Chern class. The goal of this paper to provide a relatively accessible and integrated introduction to the algebraic topology of spaces with Lie group actions, in both the smooth and the holomorphic category. We present detailed treatment of the basic constructions in equivariant de Rham theory and Dolbeault theory. We also discuss equivariant connections and curvature on vector bundles equipped with infinitesimal lifts, as well as the equivariant first Chern class of line bundles with inﬁnitesimal lifts. A novel feature of this presentation is the deﬁnition of infinitesimal lift via differential operators on the vector bundles.
